title: Seven requires_code_verification items closed by code-fact review (G0 freeze)
reviewMethod: Every item was checked against real source, types, schemas, repositories, services, IPC surfaces, tests, and call relationships at the baseline commit. No keyword-only guessing: each conclusion lists the exact paths, symbols, schemas, tests, or call sites. Absent capabilities are recorded as verified_absent, never left unresolved.

items.question: Which entities, tables, schemas, or files express Evidence today? Is there one canonical Evidence aggregate and one canonical write path, or multiple write paths that could bypass the Kernel? Which paths are production, and which are tests, fixtures, or legacy compatibility?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: Two distinct Evidence concepts exist at baseline. (a) The research-domain aggregate argument_evidence (id prefix revd_, migration 015) with kind, state (current/stale/disputed), inference capacity, provenance, and claim/mechanism support links; its repository (createArgumentGraphRepositories) exposes create/compareAndSwap, but no production caller writes it: ResearchObjectWorkspaceService, SestinaCore, pilots, appeals, rooms, and Memory only read it, and the server only exposes read-only list/detail routes. (b) The legacy task-scoped ledger evidence_items plus situation_assertions and claims (migrations 001/012) with EvidenceService in @sestina/evidence; its only importers are its own tests and the read-only legacy-import scanner. Writes to either aggregate exist only in tests and in the synthetic UI fixture helper. The v0.2.0 UI, CLI, MCP, Skills, and Provider have no production Evidence write command; the word 'evidence' also appears in non-canonical uses (Receipt evidenceClass with countsAsExternalEvidence fixed false, pilot evidence export diagnostics). Conclusion: there is no unique production Evidence write entry today; two aggregates exist in the schema.
items.targetRequirement: argument_evidence (revd_) is frozen as the single canonical Evidence aggregate. The add_evidence effect handler (G4/G6) becomes the only production writer, reusing the existing provenance, state, inference-capacity, and support-link rules. Legacy evidence_items/situation_assertions/claims become read-only migration and legacy-import sources; they are never canonical and never dual-written. Receipts never auto-promote to Evidence.

items.question: Which persistence objects does one research-state modification touch today? Is there a database transaction, a Unit of Work, a snapshot, a revision guard, or compare-and-swap? Can a canonical mutation, Receipt, Trace, Review terminal state, or revision partially succeed, and what does a process interruption leave behind?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: Present pieces: all repositories share one StorageDatabase instance (createResearchStore), ResearchUnitOfWork.commit wraps a unit in withTransaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, rollback on error, savepoints for nesting, strictly synchronous); repositories expose compareAndSwap with expected-version checks (requireExpectedNext); ResearchRoomService.commit writes direction-changed Brief proposal plus version plus Receipt inside one UoW transaction, and rollback does the same. Absent pieces: there is no projectStateRevision head or event chain, no global revision guard, and no persistent interactive Review (pending/in-flight/analyzed are in-memory Maps; only the terminal Receipt persists). A crash before commit loses the whole Review stage; a crash between commit and renderer response is resolved by Receipt existence only. There is no single transaction covering canonical object, revision, Review terminal, Receipt, and Trace because those concepts do not exist yet as one unit, so the target atomic canonical mutation is verified_absent while the per-command transaction/CAS/UoW building blocks are verified_present.
items.targetRequirement: G3 extends ResearchUnitOfWork so one commit transaction covers resulting object(s), revision head/event advance, Review terminal state, Receipt, and Trace with fault injection proving all-or-nothing. Every canonical repository write requires a transaction context (architecture test). Reads use single-read snapshots. Reviews become persistent aggregates (research_room_reviews) so crash recovery has a durable stage to return to.

items.question: How are Evidence source credibility and Brief maturity, thresholds, states, or stages expressed today? Do they share fields, enums, or implicit concepts? Is there any path that mistakes source credibility for Brief maturity? Can the planned EvidenceThreshold enum map existing data directly, or is migration required?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: They are separate concepts with separate types and no shared enum. Evidence credibility is expressed as ResearchSource.authority (user_confirmed, user_recorded, model_proposed, system_derived, imported_unconfirmed) plus state (current/stale/disputed), inference capacity, and claim/mechanism link support status (proven/unproven/disputed/stale). The Brief has no maturity or threshold enum at all: it has currentStage (seven research stages), evidenceBoundaries as free-text EvidenceBoundaryRule entries (statement, scope, allowedSourceIds, forbiddenInferenceKinds), and no quality grade. No code path maps source credibility to Brief maturity, and no path promotes Provider verdicts into Brief state. The planned EvidenceThreshold (minimumSourceClass, requiredCorroboration, acceptedInferenceCapacity) cannot be mapped losslessly from the existing free-text evidenceBoundaries: minimumSourceClass must be defined from the canonical provenance/source classes and existing rules migrate as legacy threshold rules with explicit limitations. No shared-field misuse path exists today: that coupling is verified_absent.
items.targetRequirement: Brief gains typed EvidenceThreshold and KnownUnknown fields whose source-class enum aligns with the canonical provenance model; evidenceBoundaries migrate to legacy threshold rules marked with limitations. Provider assessment can never auto-satisfy a threshold, and coverage stays a derived hint that never blocks user authority.

items.question: Does Memory duplicate Evidence or Decision content? Does it store source object ids? What does Forget delete and not delete? Can Memory deletion break Evidence, Decision, Trace, or recovery? Can Memory be carried cross-project or into outbound context by default?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: Memory does not duplicate Evidence/Decision bodies: rows store their own user-entered content plus a project_object source holding objectKind, objectId, objectVersion, and a content fingerprint (no full object body). authorityClass is working_memory_non_authoritative, so Memory never promotes to Evidence or Decision. Forget replaces the row with an irreversible tombstone (content removed) and drops unsent in-memory memory manifests; it touches nothing else: Memory is not indexed by FTS (fts tables cover only claims/evidence_items/conversation/collaboration) and does not appear in storage search. Committed Receipt Manifests keep only included item ids/versions/content hashes, never item text. Cross-project use is blocked by project-scoped ids and queries. The gaps are: no copy inventory for managed backups (which still contain pre-forget rows), no privacy redaction ledger for already-sent payloads, no Provider-side-copy disclosure, and no restore-time resurrection guard. Content duplication itself is verified_absent; the copy-boundary inventory is a target-only capability.
items.targetRequirement: G2/G7 add the forget copy inventory and privacy redaction ledger: DB/FTS/cache cleanup in one transaction with forget, managed-backup inventory, Receipt/Manifest hash-only preservation, explicit Provider-side and manual-copy non-control disclosure, and restore-time redaction checks. never_send stays a Kernel hard rule; selection stays per-item and per-Review.

items.question: What can each external interface (MCP, Skill, CLI) read and write? Can any of them modify canonical state directly, trigger Provider, or bypass Review and Authority? Is Agent Corrector an active product capability, a historical branch capability, an experiment, or not wired at all?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: No interface can bypass the Kernel. MCP exposes exactly two read-only tools (health, get_research_context) with a capability policy write=false; it can neither mutate canonical state nor trigger Provider. The sestina-research-integrity Skill is instruction-only and calls the read-only MCP plus the deterministic review CLI; it holds no runtime authority or persistence. The CLI embeds SestinaCore directly and can execute canonical commands (issue resolve/waive/dispute/reopen, Brief changes) with a user actor plus explicit --yes confirmation; these flow through the same Core authority checks and CAS, so the CLI is a user-authority transport, not a bypass. Agent Corrector is not part of this tree at the baseline: integrations/skills/canonical contains only research-integrity.md; the agent-corrector bundle exists only on the post-release branch codex/agent-corrector (commit 74c62c5f4ab22cc8267a4edc74cfaa34b078a3a8). Direct canonical writes, Provider triggering, or Review/Authority bypass by any of these interfaces is verified_absent.
items.targetRequirement: MCP stays read-only; Skills stay draft-only; CLI commands map to the same typed effect handlers with the same authority policy; the Host bridge (new, disabled by default) may only submit Review drafts. Agent Corrector merges at G7 as a companion Skill with ephemeral, explicit-handoff-only semantics and no Authority.

items.question: Is there a migration journal and a schema version? Can interrupted migrations recover? Is copy-on-write supported? Is there an atomic swap after validation? Is there dual-write? Is there rollback or read-only recovery, and what is still missing before G1?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: Present: a DB-internal migration journal (migrations table with started/completed/failed, runtime version, backup path/hash, error code, timestamps); schema version equals the highest manifest migration (20 at baseline, manifest order verified against implementations); forward-only; a failed migration for an unknown version blocks writes, known failures are retried; each migration runs in its own transaction and must be idempotent; a hashed database backup precedes each destructive migration on an existing database; too_new fails closed. Restore has verified staging plus atomic rename swap with WAL cleanup; Recovery validates DB integrity, schema, project identity, and Brief binding for multi-file restore. Absent: migration itself is in-place, not copy-on-write (no staging copy, validation, then swap for migrations); the journal is DB-internal, so a staging copy cannot be recognized from outside; there is no migration-level rollback (failure keeps the pre-migration backup, not a rewind); no dual-write exists anywhere. Missing before G1: external/maintenance journal for staging recognition, copy-on-write migration pipeline with verified staging and atomic swap, revision head/event and Review/Manifest binding validation, and the 021-025 schema set.
items.targetRequirement: G2 implements copy-on-write migration: read-only dry run, verified pre-migration backup, copy to staging, idempotent 021-025 in staging, full validation (integrity, project identity, Brief binding, revision/event chain, projections, privacy), atomic swap, reopen verification, and recovery that keeps the original database untouched until the swap. Dual-write stays forbidden; downgrade is restore of the pre-migration backup only.

items.question: What are the Provider request DNS, proxy, address validation, and redirect policies? Is there an SSRF or local-address boundary? What are the static asset path and packaged path assumptions? Where does the loopback preview end and the target Electron desktop begin? How are keys stored, and what happens when system secure storage is unavailable - can it fall back to plaintext on disk?
items.currentImplementationConclusion: Provider endpoints are validated at configuration time: external providers require HTTPS; explicit loopback may be HTTP; credentials, query, and fragments are rejected; private/metadata/link-local literals (RFC1918, 169.254.x.x, 100.64/10, multicast, metadata hostnames, IPv6 equivalents) are rejected; the request itself uses redirect=error, retry=0, size caps, and a timeout; no proxy or custom DNS dispatcher exists in the adapter, so DNS resolution and connection are delegated to the runtime fetch with no connect-time address pinning. The loopback preview server binds 127.0.0.1 only, requires a loopback Host header (421 otherwise), session tokens for mutations, and CSP/COOP/frame-deny headers; static assets are served only from the packaged client asset root with traversal and non-asset paths rejected. Secrets go to OS secure stores (DPAPI, Keychain, Secret Service) via @sestina/secrets; when the store is unavailable the system throws secure_storage_unavailable and refuses to save - there is no plaintext fallback path. The config file stores no key. Target Electron boundary: typed preload IPC, renderer without Node/secret/filesystem access, production UI with no public HTTP listener; that desktop shell does not exist at baseline (apps/ contains cli and research-room only). Connect-time DNS/address pinning and explicit proxy policy are absent today and are frozen as a G10 security gate.
items.targetRequirement: G10 must add connect-time DNS resolution and address pinning (or a controlled transport with address policy), an explicit proxy policy, and the Electron IPC threat model. Until then the current configuration-time checks plus redirect=error remain the guard with the DNS-rebinding limitation documented, and the loopback preview keeps its current identity. Secret behavior stays fail-closed: no silent plaintext persistence at any point.
